scenario: Caldera Machinery imported industrial pumps on January 10, 2024, paying $20,000 in duties. On August 5, 2025, the company re-exported the identical pumps to a buyer abroad and filed a drawback claim. The pumps were stored in a bonded warehouse during the intervening period.
policy: An importer may recover (drawback) 99% of the duties paid on imported goods if those goods are subsequently re-exported in the same condition within three years of the date of importation. Drawback is available only for goods that were not used domestically before re-export; any domestic use forfeits the drawback claim.
question: Is Caldera entitled to recover 99% of the duties paid?
